title: Io parlo, tu lavori: i verbi in -are
summary: Present tense of regular -are verbs (parlare, lavorare, abitare) and Italian's subject-drop

blocks.title: Il motore regolare: i verbi in -are
blocks.body: Most Italian verbs end in **-are**, and they all conjugate the same way. Take **parlare** (to speak): *parlo, parli, parla, parliamo, parlate, parlano*. Notice the ending already tells you **who** — that's why Italian usually **drops the subject pronoun**: *parlo italiano*, not *io parlo italiano*.
blocks.callout: The ending IS the subject. Pronouns are for emphasis, not for grammar.

blocks.title: Altri verbi in -are
blocks.body: Same pattern, new meanings: **lavorare** (to work), **abitare** (to live somewhere), **studiare** (to study), **guardare** (to watch/look at), **ascoltare** (to listen to). Swap the ending onto any of these and you're conjugating.

pairs.note: Drop the pronoun by default; bring it back only to contrast two people.

blocks.explain: **lavoriamo** — the -iamo ending is the same for every regular -are verb.

blocks.title: Costruisci una frase
blocks.prompt: Build a sentence: who + the -are verb, then where.
Write three sentences about what you and people you know do — pick from lavorare, abitare, studiare, guardare, ascoltare.
starters: Il mio amico / La mia amica...
